entities.summary: Admiral-General Luis Carrero Blanco was a Spanish Navy officer and politician. A long-time confidant and right-hand man of dictator Francisco Franco, Carrero served as Prime Minister of Spain. Upon graduating from the naval academy Carrero Blanco participated in the Rif War, and later the Spanish Civil War, in which he supported the Nationalist faction. He became one of the most prominent figures in Francoist Spain's power structure and held throughout his career a number of high-ranking offices such as those of Undersecretary of the Presidency from 1941 to 1967 and Franco's deputy from 1967 to 1973.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As Prime Minister of Spain from 1967 to 1973, Luis Carrero Blanco played a crucial role in maintaining Francoist power structure and implementing economic reforms. His leadership had significant regional impact on Spanish politics and economy.
